newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates stable, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates stable, seen firm.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates remained stable on Wednesday on buying by mills and will remain firm as demand is higher than supplies, dealers said.

"The recent rains in the Punjab province have affected the quality of cotton there and slowed down its supplies," dealer Shamimul Haq said. "The cotton from Sindh province is in demand by mills in Punjab because its quality is good."
He said cotton prices would remain firm because of the shortage of ready stocks. "The arrival of fresh supplies from the new (1997/98 is likely to pick up from mid-August.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted from 2,200 ($54.16) to 2,225 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
